scenarios.intent: An agent wants one page as clean text so it can answer a question about it without menus and footers in the way.
scenarios.outcome: The reply gives the low tide time from the article, 12:31.
scenarios.prompt: Read the page {origin}/article. What time is low tide? Reply in one line with the time.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants web search results it can follow, so it can find pages about a topic.
scenarios.outcome: The reply names the first search hit, the fixture page /a.
scenarios.prompt: Search the web for "alpha story" (source: web). Reply with the URL of the first result.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants a short answer tied to the page it came from, so the user can trust and check it.
scenarios.outcome: The reply gives the high tide time, 06:12, and cites the page /tides.
scenarios.prompt: Answer the question "When is high tide at the north pier?" using only the source {origin}/tides. Reply with the time and the source URL you cited.
reference: When is high tide at the north pier?

scenarios.intent: An agent wants named fields from a product page as data, so it can fill a table without reading the page itself.
scenarios.outcome: The reply gives the price $19.99 and the sku W-100 read from the page.
scenarios.prompt: From {origin}/product, extract the fields title (selector h1), price (selector .price) and sku (selector .sku). Reply with the price and the sku.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants every URL on a site before it reads any of them, so it can plan what to fetch.
scenarios.outcome: The reply lists the site's pages /a, /b and /c.
scenarios.prompt: Map the site {origin}/ and list every URL you found, one per line.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants the content of every page on a small site, so it can study the whole site at once.
scenarios.outcome: The reply names all five page titles: Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta and Epsilon.
scenarios.prompt: Crawl {origin}/ to depth 2 (at most 10 pages). Reply with the title of every page you crawled.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants to know when a page it watches really changes, so it can alert the user only about what is new.
scenarios.outcome: The reply says the fare changed to 4 dollars.
scenarios.prompt: Check the page {origin}/notice for changes twice in a row, using the monitor database {tmp}/monitor.sqlite both times. Reply with what changed between the two checks.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants the items of a news feed in order, so it can follow updates without scraping pages.
scenarios.outcome: The reply lists the feed items Alpha, Beta and Gamma, in that order.
scenarios.prompt: Read the feed {origin}/feed.xml. Reply with the item titles in the order the feed lists them, one per line.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants a topic researched across sources in one step, so it gets findings with the pages behind them.
scenarios.outcome: The reply names the fixture page /a as a source the research used.
scenarios.prompt: Research the topic "alpha story". Reply with the source URLs the research used.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants a long text cut to its key sentences with no model call, so it saves tokens and gets the same result each time.
scenarios.outcome: The reply contains a summary sentence about the north pier taken word for word from the text.

eval.answerMatches: The north pier floods at high tide\.|High tide at the north pier is at 06:12\.

scenarios.prompt: Summarize this text to 2 sentences: "Tides rise twice a day. The north pier floods at high tide. Gulls nest on the breakwater. High tide at the north pier is at 06:12." Reply with the summary exactly as the tool returned it.
reference: Tides rise twice a day. The north pier floods at high tide. Gulls nest on the breakwater. High tide at the north pier is at 06:12.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants a clear error when a page is gone, so it can tell the user instead of guessing.
scenarios.outcome: The reply says the page was not found (HTTP 404).
scenarios.prompt: Read the page {origin}/gone. Reply with what happened, including the HTTP status if there was one.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants many pages read in one call and told which ones failed, so one bad URL does not hide the good results.
scenarios.outcome: The reply names /binary as the URL that failed.
scenarios.prompt: Read these pages in one batch: {origin}/a, {origin}/b, {origin}/binary. Reply with the URL that failed.

scenarios.intent: An agent wants several pages read with one tool call, so it does not spend a call and a turn on each URL.
scenarios.outcome: One batch call reads every URL, no scrape call runs, and the reply names /binary as the URL that failed.
scenarios.prompt: Read these pages: {origin}/a, {origin}/b, {origin}/binary. Reply with the URL that failed.
